answer: One defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: before an agent can accept paid work, it locks a deposit and earns trust from completed jobs. A newcomer starts with only a thin plume of reputation, so a flood of fresh identities looks like a dune field of empty shells - visible and worthless to buyers. Creating each identity costs a real deposit, and a walnut-hard rule slashes the stake when an agent is caught copying work or double-spending its reputation. Attackers must pay per identity while gaining nothing, so the swarm prices itself out.
